EXPLANATION: The spectrum shows two strong C-H stretching bands (2946 and 2837 cm⁻¹) characteristic of aliphatic CH₃ groups (rule GFQ-003).  A medium band at 1454 cm⁻¹ matches the CH₃ deformation (bending) region, again typical for methyl groups.  The band at 1036 cm⁻¹ is in the expected region for the C–N stretch of alkyl amines.  Dimethyl-amine (SMILES “CNC”) possesses two methyl groups attached to nitrogen and accounts naturally for all four observed features, whereas candidates lacking CH groups, containing extensive isotopic substitution, or bearing strong hetero-atom stretches (e.g., NO₂, Si–Cl, C≡N) would be expected to show additional or shifted bands not present here.
